title: Restoring the Green Spaces of Hackney
description: Join fellow volunteers for a morning of litter picking, path clearing and wildflower sowing across the marshes. All tools, gloves and refreshments are provided — just bring sturdy boots and a rain jacket in case of drizzle.
location: Hackney Marshes, main car park, Hackney

title: A Cleaner Thames, Together
description: We will be cleaning the river foreshore at low tide, collecting plastic waste, bottles and scraps of metal before they wash back out with the tide. Litter pickers and gloves are provided, and a full safety briefing runs before we head onto the mud.

title: Community Gardens of Brixton
description: Help the local growing crew prepare raised beds for the winter and plant garlic, onion sets and broad beans. There will be a hot soup lunch at midday and a short composting workshop for anyone keen to learn soil basics.

title: Urban Rewilding in Camden
description: A practical rewilding session beside the canal: building log pile habitats, planting a native hedge and digging the edge of a small pond for frogs and newts. Families are welcome, and the session ends with hot chocolate by the fire pit.

title: Richmond Park Conservation Day
description: A full day working alongside the royal park's conservation team to clear invasive bracken and cut back encroaching scrub from historic grasslands. Lunch break at noon; please wear long sleeves and bring plenty of water.

title: Greenwich Riverside Restoration
description: Help restore the planted embankments along the riverside walk: weeding, mulching the new beds and replanting salt-tolerant species damaged by the summer's storms. A gentle session suitable for first-time volunteers.

title: Hampstead Heath Meadow Day
description: Sow a new hay meadow on the Heath's eastern slopes and rake in yellow rattle seed to weaken invasive grasses. Expect beautiful views from the Parliament Hill ridge and a guided autumn walk after the work is done.

title: Peckham Community Tree Planting
description: Plant sixty whips — rowan, hawthorn and blackthorn — along a housing estate's green corridor. Spades and gloves are provided, and a local arborist will teach proper planting technique so the young trees thrive for decades.
location: Peckham Rye Park café gates, Southwark

title: Winter Beds at Walthamstow
description: Get the community garden tucked in before the frost: mulching beds with leaf mould, wrapping tender plants and sowing winter salad under cover. Warm drinks and biscuits provided throughout the morning.
location: Walthamstow Marshes, south gate, Waltham Forest

title: Deptford Creekside Clean-up
description: A big push to clear plastic and litter from the Deptford Creek reeds before winter birds arrive. Wear wellingtons — we provide waders for anyone crossing the shallows — and finish with tea at the creek-side hut.

title: Islington Pocket Parks Project
description: We are turning three neglected corners of Islington into mini wildlife gardens. Help plant shade-loving ferns and bulbs, install bird boxes and brighten walls with climbing plants. No experience needed, tools supplied.

title: Wandle Way Willow Planting
description: Plant living willow stakes along the River Wandle's eroded banks to stabilise the soil and shade the water for trout. Mud guaranteed, satisfaction guaranteed too — bring a change of trousers.

title: Epping Forest Edge Restoration
description: Work with the forest keepers to coppice hazel and widen woodland rides so butterflies and dormice can flourish. A great one for anyone curious about traditional woodland craft — bow saws and gloves provided.
location: High Beach visitor centre, Waltham Forest

title: Battersea Park Bulb Planting
description: Help the park gardeners plant twenty thousand tulip and daffodil bulbs for a dazzling spring display along the lakeside walks. A fast, cheerful job made better with mince pies at the tea break.
location: Battersea Park gate, Albert Bridge side, Wandsworth

title: Westminster Wildlife Corridors
description: Link two green spaces through a new wildlife corridor: planting berry-bearing shrubs and creating dead-wood habitat for stag beetles. Learn how small urban connections can make a big difference for biodiversity.
location: St John's Wood Church Gardens, Westminster

title: Tower Hamlets Tool School
description: A free workshop for volunteers who want to care for tools as much as gardens: sharpening spades, oiling loppers and repairing wheelbarrows, all while sharing plans for next season's growing projects.
location: Mile End Park, Ecology Pavilion, Tower Hamlets

title: Brent Reservoir Bird Habitat
description: Cut and pile reeds at the reservoir's wetland edge to open feeding grounds for wintering wildfowl. Waterproof boots are essential and an expert-led session on local bird ID runs afterwards for those interested.

title: Haringey Hedgerow Heroes
description: Plant two hundred metres of new hedgerow along a school boundary — hawthorn, hazel, spindle and dog rose. Once grown, it will shelter the playground from wind and feed birds through the winter.

title: Ealing Orchard Revival
description: Prune and mulch the centenary community orchard's apple and pear trees with an expert from London's orchard collective. Learn winter pruning skills you can take home to your own garden.

title: Bexley Saltmarsh Restoration
description: Restore the saltmarsh fringe of the Crayford marshes by planting samphire and sea purslane, buffer habitat for rare harvesting mice. A brilliant session for birders — waders, gloves and a flask of cocoa provided.

title: Winter Coat & Blanket Drive
description: Sort, repair and bag donated winter coats and blankets for our partner shelters across the city. Warm drinks and good music provided all afternoon.
location: St John Community Hall, Bethnal Green
